title: Berbere Spiced Rockfish
text:
# Berbere Spiced Rockfish

## Description
This one’s fast, flavorful, and built to impress.The key is the batter — punched up with berbere, an Ethiopian spice blend packed with dried chilies, garlic, ginger, paprika, and all kinds of warm, earthy depth.
I like to use rockfish I catch off the coast of San Diego, but any white, flaky fish like halibut, cod, or snapper, would taste great.



Ingredients
1/2 cup all-purpose flour
1 1/2 tablespoons berbere spice
1 (12-ounce) can cold beer 
Oil, for frying
4 pickle slices, finely chopped
4 tablespoons mayo

1 pound rockfish fillet, cut into portions


Preparation

Start by making your batter. In a mixing bowl, combine flour and 1 tablespoon of berbere spice. Slowly whisk in cold beer until a thick, smooth Think pancake batter with a little attitude.

Heat oil in a deep pan or wok to 350°F — just enough to submerge the fish.

While the oil heats, make the tartar sauce. Combine pickles, mayo, and ½ tablespoon of berbere in a small bowl. Mix well and set aside. Add a pinch of smoked shoyu salt if you’ve got it — it adds a rich, savory hit that works great with fried fish.

oat the fish pieces fully in the batter, then carefully slide them into the pan. Fry until golden and crispy, about 1–2 minutes depending on thickness.  145°F.

erve hot with a spoonful of berbere tartar sauce on the side.

title: Bluefin Tuna Butter Masala
text:
# Bluefin Tuna Butter Masala

## Description
Butter chicken may be the gold standard of Indian comfort food, but this twist with fresh bluefin tuna brings a fresh coastal twist. The sauce is built on caramelized onion, garlic, ginger, and warm spices, rounded out with tomato, yogurt, and butter for that signature silky finish. Quick-seared peppers and tuna add freshness and depth, creating a dish that feels indulgent yet light. Served with rice or roti, it’s a catch-and-cook recipe that proves butter masala belongs far beyond the chicken pot.

Ingredients

1/2 onion, chopped
1 whole garlic bulb, peeled
1/4-inch piece fresh ginger, minced
1/2 tablespoon garam masala
2 teaspoons degi mirch (or Kashmiri chili powder)
1/2 cup plain yogurt
1/2 stick unsalted butter (4 tablespoons)
2 bell peppers, chopped
1/2 tablespoon turmeric
Salt, to taste
Fresh cilantro, for garnish
Preparation
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. dd the onion and cook until translucent, tir in the ginger, garam masala, and degi mirch. Sauté until the mixture begins to caramelize and release its aroma. Add the tomatoes and cook until they soften and release their liquid, then stir in the yogurt and butter. Blend the mixture with an immersion blender until smooth, adding water if needed to achieve a silky sauce.
In a separate pan, heat a little oil over high heat. Add the bell peppers and sauté until just tender. Push them to the side of the pan, add the turmeric, then sear the tuna quickly until browned. Pour in the  and reduce the heat to low immer for 2–3 minutes until cooked through.
Finish with a scatter of fresh cilantro and serve hot with steamed rice or warm roti.

title: Bourbon and Earl Grey Tea Cured Tuna
text:
# Bourbon and Earl Grey Tea Cured Tuna

## Description
This recipe is a sophisticated and flavorful way to enjoy tuna. The tuna is first cured with a blend of salt, brown sugar, Earl Grey tea leaves, and bourbon, and togarashi, an all-purpose seasoning blend from Japan known for [description]. The cure imparts a balanced sweetness, aromatic depth, and a subtle kick of heat to the fish. 
Once cured, the tuna is paired with homemade tapioca crisps, which are created by cooking and dehydrating tapioca pearls mixed with squid ink and togarashi. The crisps are then fried to a perfect crunch. 
The final dish features diced cured tuna topped on the crisp, with optional garnishes like pickled chilies and chives. This elegant appetizer marries rich, complex flavors with a delightful texture, making it a standout choice for special occasions or an indulgent treat. 



Ingredients
Tuna Cure: 
200g non-iodized salt (see note)
70g brown sugar (see note)
2 tablespoons togarashi
2 packets Earl Grey tea, opened 
4 tablespoons bourbon of choice
Tuna:
1 pound of tuna fillets 
1 tablespoons soy sauce 
Tapioca Crisp: 
1/2 cup tapioca pearls 
1 tablespoon squid ink
1 tablespoon togarashi
Oil, for frying (I prefer Chosen Foods avocado oil) 
Preparation
In a medium bowl, combine the salt, brown sugar, togarashi, Earl Grey tea leaves, and bourbon, mixing until the texture resembles wet sand. Lay the tuna on a sheet of plastic wrap and generously coat it with the cure mixture, turn and coat the other side, ensuring even coverage. Wrap the tuna tightly in the plastic wrap.

Place the tuna in a tray to catch any moisture, then set a heavy plate or skillet on top and gently press down. Transfer to the refrigerator and allow the tuna to cure for 8-12 hours for optimal results. 

To make the tapioca crisps: Preheat the oven to 175°F. In a large saucepan, combine 2 1/2 cups water and the tapioca pearls. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat and cook until the pearls turn translucent, about X minutes. Once cooked, transfer the tapioca to a strainer and rinse thoroughly to remove excess starch. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Stir in the squid ink and togarashi until fully incorporated. Spread the mixture in a thin layer on the prepared baking tray and bake until fully dehydrated, 2-3 hours. 

Allow the tapioca to cool for 5-10 minutes. Meanwhile, line a plate with paper towels. Use your hands to break the tapioca into X-size pieces. Next, pour X inch of oil into a large skillet and heat over medium-high until 375°F (190°C). Fry the tapioca crisps one at a time, watching closely as they will puff up within seconds. Transfer finished crisps to the paper towel-lined plate.
Lastly, assemble the dish: Dice the cured tuna after rinsing off any remaining cure and add it to a large bowl. Add the soy sauce and toss until evenly coated. Place the seasoned tuna on top of the tapioca crisps. Feel free to garnish with your favorite toppings—I prefer pickled chilies and chives.

Note: I find the most consistent results when I use metric weights for this recipe. You’re welcome to estimate or use cups instead. 200g of salt is about 2/3 cup. For brown sugar, it varies based on if you’re using light or dark (dark is heavier, thus you need slightly less) and if you’re packing it or not. Overall, you’re looking at just a smidge under 1/3 cup if you’re using packed light brown sugar.

title: Braised Lingcod in Ginger Soy Broth
text:
# Braised Lingcod in Ginger Soy Broth

## Description
This recipe is a versatile and elegant way to highlight the delicate flavors of mild white fish such as lingcod, halibut, or rockfish. Poaching the fish in a fragrant broth of soy sauce, ginger, and green onions keeps it tender, moist, and deeply flavorful. It’s served over a bed of rice—but not just any rice—this one is gently simmered with cardamom, kaffir lime leaves, and whole peppercorns, infusing it with warm spice, citrusy perfume, and a gentle peppery bite. The final flourish is a pour of hot oil over fresh herbs, releasing their aroma in a fragrant sizzle that makes the whole dish come alive.




Ingredients
2 pounds Lingcod or Rockfish
Rice: 
1 cup rice
3 black cardamom pods
1 tablespoon peppercorns
4 kaffir lime leaves (see Note)
Broth: 
1/4 cup soy sauce
 piece ginger
1 bunchsliced green onions, white and green parts
2 tablespoons oil (such as vegetable or coconut)
Fresh cilantro, leaves and stems, for serving 
Pickled chilies, for serving
Preparation
Start by placing 1 cup of rice, 1 cup of water, cardamom, peppercorns, and kaffir lime leaves in an Instant Pot. Pressure cook on low for 12 minutes, allowing the device to naturally release for 10 minutes after cooking. 

Meanwhile, in a shallow pan, add just enough water to cover your fish and season it with soy sauce, ginger, and the whites of green onions. Bring this mixture to a light simmer over medium-low heat. Carefully add the fish and cook until its internal temperature reaches 140 degrees Fahrenheit. Transfer the fish and broth to a serving dish. Next, arrange the remaining green onions over the fish along with the cilantro. 

Next, add the oil to a small skillet and heat over high heat until it begins to smoke. Immediately remove the pan from the heat and carefully pour the hot oil over the fish. It will sizzle and may splatter so be cautious. The oil will infuse the herbs with its heat. For an optional touch, add pickled chilies over the fish for a tangy and spicy complement. Finally, serve the fish and its broth over the fragrant rice and enjoy the harmonious blend of flavors.

Note: Kaffir lime leaf can be purchased at any  grocery store or online.

title: Butter Keema
text:
# Butter Keema

## Description
You’ve probably heard of butter chicken — the iconic North Indian dish known for its rich, creamy sauce and tender pieces of chicken swimming in buttery, spiced gravy. It's a modern classic for a reason: comforting, bold, and impossible to stop eating once you start.
This version takes everything people love about butter chicken but swaps in ground wild boar for a deeper, gamey flavor that holds up beautifully against the sauce. If you've got ground game meat in the freezer, this is one of the best ways to turn it into something familiar but just different enough to make it yours.
We’ll start by building a butter masala sauce from scratch — simple, layered, and full of soul — then fold in the cooked ground boar to finish. Serve it hot over rice or with roti to scoop up every last drop.

## Ingredients

**For the Keema:**
1 lb ground wild boar (or ground venison, elk, etc.)
2 tablespoons garam masala
Salt to taste
1 small bunch curry leaves
Oil for cooking

**For the Butter Masala:**
2 tablespoons butter
1 teaspoon mustard seeds
1 teaspoon cumin seeds
1 teaspoon salt (adjust to taste)
1 onion, finely chopped
4 cloves garlic, minced
3–4 tomatoes, chopped
1 teaspoon turmeric
A pinch of hing (asafoetida)
½ cup cream

## Preparation

**Make the Butter Masala Sauce:**
In a heavy pan, melt the butter over medium heat. Add mustard seeds and cumin seeds, letting them pop and release their aroma. Stir in the onion, salt, and garlic. Cook until the onions soften and begin to caramelize.

Add the tomatoes, turmeric, and a pinch of hing. Let everything cook down until the tomatoes fully break apart and the mixture thickens into a rough paste. Add a cup of water and blend the mixture until smooth. Stir in the cream and blend once more until silky. Set the sauce aside.

**Cook the Boar:**
In a pan over medium heat, add a little oil and the curry leaves and toast until fragrant. Add the ground boar, season with garam masala and salt, and cook over medium-high heat until the meat is browned.

**Assemble:**
Once the boar is cooked through and deeply browned, pour the butter masala sauce over the meat. Stir everything together and let it simmer for a few minutes to bring the flavors together.

Top with fresh cilantro, fried onions, and a squeeze of lime. Serve hot with rice or roti.

title: Cambodian-Style Deer Tenderloin
text:
# Cambodian-Style Deer Tenderloin

## Description
In Siem Reap, I savored Cambodian roast chicken marinated in soy and fish sauce, garlic, fire-roasted, and glazed with oyster sauce. It was charred to perfection and enjoyed with delectable pepper sauce. These sweet, salty, funky, umami bomb flavors inspired this recipe. It’s an interesting way to showcase the flavors of Cambodia combined with some modern techniques.
For this recipe, I would recommend following the sous vide method, but you can prepare it in the oven or over a grill just fine. I also recommend buying Kampot pepper. It may be pricey, but it is by far the best pepper in the world. 



Ingredients
Venison backstrap or tenderloin 
Compound Butter: 
1 cup (2 sticks) butter, softened 
3 tablespoons garlic cloves 
2 tablespoons soy sauce 
2 tablespoons fish sauce 
2 tablespoons freshly cracked Kampot pepper 
Tuk Meric (pepper sauce): 
1/4 cup Kampot pepper 
1/4 cup freshly squeezed lime juice (from 3 limes)
2 teaspoons sugar 
2 teaspoons salt 
Glaze: 
3 tablespoons oyster sauce 
2 tablespoons soy sauce 
2 tablespoons rice wine vinegar 
5 teaspoons minced garlic
1/2 tablespoon sugar 
Preparation
Preheat your sous vide bath to 120°F (see note). In a medium bowl, mix together the butter, garlic, soy sauce, fish sauce, and pepper until combined. Spread it all over your backstrap/tenderloin. Transfer the tenderloin to a ziplock or vacuum-seal bag and seal. Add the bag to the water bath and cook, undisturbed, for 3 hours. 

Meanwhile, make the Tuk Meric (Cambodian pepper sauce). Toast the Kampot peppercorns until they become fragrant. Transfer to a heatproof mortar and pestle and roughly crush. In a small bowl, combine the salt, sugar, and lime juice. Whisk until no particles remain. Stir in the pepper and set aside.

Next, make the glaze. In a medium bowl, whisk together the oyster sauce, soy sauce,  seasoned rice wine vinegar, garlic, and sugar. 

Remove the bag from the water bath using tongs. Open the bag and lather the venison with the glaze. Finish the backstrap over hot coals, constantly brushing the glaze. Once the venison reaches an internal temperature of 130-135°F, it’s done! Slice and  serve on a platter or large plate with the Tuk Meric in a bowl in the middle. 

Note: No sous vide? No worries! Preheat your oven to 225°F and add the venison to a [preferred equipment such as baking dish or sheet] and cook until the internal temperature reads °F on an instant-read thermometer, about  .

title: Crispy Lingcod with Creamy Tomato Polenta & Cilantro Sauce
text:
# Crispy Lingcod with Creamy Tomato Polenta & Cilantro Sauce

## Description
This dish is all about balance — crispy fish, creamy polenta, bright green sauce, and just enough heat. Lingcod has a mild, slightly sweet flavor that holds up beautifully when fried. The polenta adds richness and cilantro sauce brings a fresh, zesty kick that cuts through everything. It’s cozy, bold, and easy to riff on



Ingredients
Lingcod:
1 lingcod fillets
1 t salt
1 t MSG (optional)
Avocado oil, for shallow frying

Breading:
Panko breadcrumbs

2 eggs, whisked


Creamy Tomato Polenta:
1 cup polenta

1 cup milk
½ cup shredded cheddar cheese
1 white onion, finely chopped
1 bunch cilantro stems, finely chopped
2 medium tomatoes, pureed
4 cloves garlic, minced
Seasoning of choice

Cilantro Sauce:
⅓ cup mayo
Juice of 1 lemon
1 bunch cilantro leaves
1 jalapeño (or serrano/habanero for more heat)
4 cloves garlic, minced


Quick Pickled Jalapeños (optional):
1 jalapeño, thinly sliced
½ cup red wine vinegar

Preparation


Bread and Fry the Fish
Season  with salt and MSG. Let the rest while you prep your dredging station. 


Dip each fillet into the egg, then press into the panko. For extra crunch, double-dip: egg → panko → egg → panko again. Shallow fry in avocado oil over medium-high heat until golden and crispy on both sides. Internal temp should hit 145°F.

Make the Polenta Base
Bring 4 cups of water to a boil. Stir in the polenta and cook for about 10 minutes, stirring often, until thick.

Meanwhile, make the sofrito: In a skillet, sauté onion, garlic, and chopped cilantro stems in oil until soft. Add your seasoning and the pureed tomatoes. Cook until most of the moisture evaporates and the mixture thickens.

Stir milk and cheddar into the cooked polenta until smooth. Fold in the tomato sofrito and mix until fully incorporated.

Blend the Cilantro Sauce
In a jar or blender, combine mayo, lemon juice, cilantro leaves, jalapeño, and garlic. Blend until smooth with an immersion blender or standard blender. Thin with a splash of water or more lemon juice if needed.

Quick Pickle the Jalapeños (Optional)
Place thinly sliced jalapeños in a small jar or bowl. Cover with red wine vinegar and  30 minutes.

To Plate
Spoon a generous layer of creamy tomato polenta onto each plate. Top with a crispy lingcod fillet. Drizzle with cilantro sauce and add a few pickled jalapeños if you want that extra bite.

title: Desi Deer Flatbread
text:
# Desi Deer Flatbread

## Description
This Indian-inspired flatbread recipe is a culinary adventure that transforms familiar ingredients into an exotic and flavorful experience. 

A harmonious blend of cauliflower, thinly sliced red onion, and ground venison forms the base, spiced with garam masala. The addition of melted cheese adds a creamy richness, while a drizzle of tangy yogurt and tamarind sauce brings a refreshing finish. 

Served on crispy, toasted naan and topped with ripe tomatoes and fresh cilantro, this dish is a delightful departure from the ordinary, perfect for those seeking a unique and satisfying meal.







Ingredients
Flatbread:
2 tablespoons butter
1 cup cauliflower, cut into small florets
1 red onion, thinly sliced
Salt, to taste
1 pound ground deer
3 tablespoons garam masala
1 cup shredded cheese (such as pepperjack)
4 naan
2 ripe tomatoes, diced
Fresh cilantro, chopped
Sauce:
1/2 cup plain yogurt
2 tablespoons tamarind paste

Preparation
Begin by heating a large pan or griddle over medium heat and melting 1 tablespoon of butter to coat the surface evenly. Add the cauliflower florets and red onion, sautéing them until they achieve a desirable golden hue and seasoning them generously with salt to enhance their flavor. 
Make a space in the center of the pan and add another tablespoon of butter. Next, add the ground venison, stirring and flipping frequently until the meat is browned and cooked through, about X minutes. 
Sprinkle the garam masala over the mixture, mixing well to ensure the spices evenly coat the ingredients and allow the flavors to meld together. Once the spices have incorporated fully, sprinkle the shredded cheese over the mixture and allow it to melt slightly.
Place the naan flatbreads and cook them until they are crispy and toasted to your liking. Once the naan is toasted, remove it from the pan and spread the venison and vegetable mixture evenly over each piece. 
Top each naan with additional cheese, sliced tomatoes, and chopped cilantro. 
In a small bowl, mix the plain yogurt with tamarind paste until well combined, creating a tangy sauce. Drizzle over the assembled flatbreads and serve.

title: Desi-Style Fish Cakes
text:
# Desi-Style Fish Cakes

## Description
These fish cakes are a delightful fusion of flavors, blending the essence of classic French cuisine with bold, vibrant Indian spices. Inspired by a [fish name] I caught in the Chesapeake Bay, this recipe offers a fun twist on a popular mid-Atlantic dish. The flaky fish, infused with the aromatic notes of curry leaves during poaching, pairs…. [add mayo to this paragraph, if possible].. 
The flaky fish, infused with the aromatic notes of curry leaves during poaching, pairs perfectly with the subtle warmth of garam masala. Each crispy, golden-brown patty is crowned with a rich curry leaf velouté—a silky sauce that marries the richness of butter with the savory depth of fish stock. The velouté, with its hint of garam masala and fresh curry leaves, adds a luxurious finish to the dish, making each bite a flavorful journey. Topped with vibrant red onion and fresh cilantro, these fish cakes marry tradition with innovation, perfect for those who appreciate a bold twist on a classic.



Ingredients
Fish Cakes:
1 pound white fish fillets (such as striper)
1 red onion, finely chopped
2 tablespoons Kewpie mayo 
1/2 cup breadcrumbs (see Note)
Salt, to taste
1 tablespoon garam masala
Oil, for shallow frying
Curry Leaf Velouté:
2 tablespoons butter
2 garlic cloves, minced
2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
8-10 fresh curry leaves (see Note)
1 teaspoon garam masala
Garnish:
Fresh cilantro, chopped
Red onion, thinly sliced
Preparation
To prepare the fish cakes, start by poaching your fish in water seasoned with curry leaves. This imparts a subtle, aromatic flavor that forms the foundation of the dish. Once the fish is cooked through, remove it from the water, but don’t discard the liquid—we’ll be using it later to create the velouté sauce. Allow the fish to cool slightly, then carefully flake it, ensuring that all bones are removed. 

In a large mixing bowl, combine the flaked fish with the finely chopped red onion, Kewpie mayo, breadcrumbs, salt, and garam masala. Using your hands, form the mixture into patties of your desired size, pressing them gently to ensure they hold together. 

Pour X inch of oil into a SIZE skillet. Heat over medium heat. Once the oil shimmers, add the patties one at a time. You may need to work in batches. Cook, undisturbed, until golden brown and crispy, about 2-3 minutes. Flip and cook 2-3 minutes more or until they develop a golden-brown crust and are heated through. The exterior should be crispy.

Meanwhile, prepare the curry leaf velouté. In a medium  saucepan, melt the butter. Once bubbling, add the minced garlic and cook, stirring often, until fragrant. Whisk in flour to create a roux, cooking it briefly until it loses its raw flour taste. Gradually add the reserved fish poaching liquid 1/4 cup at a time, whisking constantly, until a total of 1 1/2 cups has been added. Cook, whisking constantly, until no lumps remain and the mixture forms a slightly thickened, smooth, velvety sauce. Remove from the heat and stir in the curry leaves and garam masala. 

To serve, place the hot, crispy fish cakes on a plate and generously ladle the curry leaf velouté over the top. Garnish with fresh cilantro and slices of red onion.

Note 1:  If the mixture is too runny to form a ball, add breadcrumbs 1 tablespoon at a time, stirring after each, until it’s wet but not sticky.
Note 2: Curry leaf can be purchases at any Indian or South Asian Store.

title: Dungeness Crab Curry
text:
# Dungeness Crab Curry

## Description
The idea for this crab curry came after a trip to the coast, where I bought the freshest, sweetest crab straight off a dockside boat. I wanted to pair that sweetness with the bold, layered flavors I grew up eating—so I simmered the crab in a rich masala of garlic, ginger, chili, turmeric, and fresh green onions. Finished with a sprinkle of cilantro, it’s a dish that celebrates both the depth of Indian cooking and the simple joy of cooking with seafood at its peak.




Ingredients
2 tablespoons canola oil or avocado oil 
2-3 Dungeness crabs (cleaned)
6 cloves garlic
3-inch piece fresh ginger 
1 red or green chili 
1 tablespoon kosher salt
1 red onion
1/2 large tomato or 1 small 
2 tablespoons garam masala
1 tablespoon turmeric
1/4 cup diced green onion 
1 bunch cilantro leaves
Preparation
To begin, thinly slice the onion, dice the tomato, and smash and peel the garlic cloves. Peel and slice the ginger, and slice the chili. Place the chili, garlic, ginger, and 1 teaspoon of kosher salt into a mortar and pestle, and grind or mash until a paste forms (the salt will help to break down the ingredients). 

Clean the crabs by breaking them into halves and removing all legs. You should have 2 claws, 6 legs, and 2 body halves per crab. Make a few cracks in the legs and claws, this will allow the masale to penetrate the meat while cooking. 

Heat the oil in a 6- or 8-quart Dutch oven or large pot over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the onions and sauté until translucent, about 2-3 minutes. Incorporate the diced tomatoes and cook for an additional 3 minutes. Next, add the ginger, garlic, and chili paste and sauté for another minute. Reduce the heat to medium-low and stir in 1/2 cup of water, as well as the turmeric, and garam masala. Continue cooking for 4-5 minutes, allowing the water to mostly evaporate and the oil to begin separating from the vegetables and masala.

Add the cleaned crab to the pot, mixing well to coat it with the masala. Cook on medium-low heat for 3 minutes. Lower the heat to low, then add 2 cups of water, as well as the green onions, and 2 teaspoons of salt. Stir well, scraping the bottom of the pan. Cover and simmer over low heat for 25 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes. Once done, turn off the heat, stir the curry, and scatter fresh cilantro leaves over the top. Let rest for 15 minutes before stirring and serving.

title: Dungeness Crab Tikki
text:
# Dungeness Crab Tikki

## Description
This recipe takes the beloved Indian street-side aloo tikki and lifts it into something indulgent with the natural sweetness of Dungeness crab. Aloo tikki is famous for its chatpatta personality—spicy, sweet, salty, and tangy all at once—what Chef Gaggan Anand calls true Indian umami. The crab folds seamlessly into that flavor bomb, adding richness and depth while keeping the soul of the tikki unmistakably classic. If fresh Dungeness isn’t in season, good lump crab meat is a perfect stand-in.


Ingredients

Title: 
12 ounces Dungeness crab meat (or lump crab meat)
4 small potatoes, boiled and mashed
2 shallots, finely chopped
2 chilies, finely chopped (adjust to spice preference)
1 tablespoon curry powder
1 tablespoon salt
1 tablespoon turmeric
1 tablespoon tamarind paste
1/2 cup Aloo Bhujia (crushed, for coating)
Oil, for frying

Preparation
Make the sauce. In a small bowl, whisk together the hili , yogurt, tamarind paste, and lime juice until smooth. Transfer to a squeeze bottle if desired for easier serving.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the crab meat, mashed potatoes, shallots, chilies, curry powder, salt, turmeric, and tamarind paste. Mix until well combined, then shape into patties about 1/2-inch thick. 
Roll each patty in crushed aloo bhujia.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the patties for 2–3 minutes per side, until golden brown and crisp. Remove and drain briefly on paper towels.
Arrange the tikkis on a serving plate and drizzle generously with the prepared sauce. Serve hot, with extra sauce on the side if desired.

title: Fish Curry with Okra and Green Beans
text:
# Fish Curry with Okra and Green Beans

## Description
This curry balances smoky grilled fish, roasted tomatoes, and spiced vegetables for a dish that feels both rustic and refined. The fish is marinated in yogurt, turmeric, and curry leaves, then grilled until charred and tender. Green beans simmer in a fragrant curry base while crispy fried okra is folded in at the end, adding texture and depth. Finished with fresh cilantro, it’s a vibrant and comforting dish that showcases Indian flavors at their best.

Ingredients


1/2 cup plain yogurt

1 teaspoon turmeric

8–10 curry leaves
Juice of 1 lime

4 tomatoes
2 tablespoons oil
1 teaspoon mustard seeds
1 onion, finely chopped
1-inch piece ginger, minced
4 garlic cloves, minced
10 curry leaves (for curry base)
1 teaspoon turmeric
1 teaspoon garam masala
1 teaspoon degi mirch (or Kashmiri chili powder)
Salt, to taste
1/2 pound green beans, trimmed
1/2 pound okra, sliced
Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

Preparation

In a large bowl, whisk together the yogurt, turmeric, curry leaves, and lime juice.  fish fillets and marinate for at least 2 hours or up to 24 hours .

Preheat a grill to medium-high. Grill the fish until lightly charred and just cooked through, about 3–4 minutes per side. Place the tomatoes on the grill alongside the fish and roast until blistered. Remove and set aside.

For the curry base, heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and let them pop, then stir in the onion, ginger, garlic, curry leaves, turmeric, garam masala, degi mirch, and salt. Cook until fragrant, about 5 minutes. Add the roasted tomatoes and green beans, along with a splash of water, and simmer until the beans are tender and the curry develops a rich, saucy consistency.

Meanwhile, fry the okra in hot oil until golden and crisp. Season lightly with salt.

To serve, add the grilled fish and fried okra to the curry base, folding gently to combine. Garnish with fresh cilantro and enjoy with warm roti, naan, or steamed rice.

title: Fish Vada Pav
text:
# Fish Vada Pav

## Description
Vada pav is one of Mumbai’s most iconic street foods—often called the “poor man’s burger”—with roots in the 1960s. Traditionally made with spiced potato fritters tucked into soft buns with chutney, it’s beloved for its bold flavor and satisfying bite. This version swaps the potato for rockfish, blending coastal flavors with the classic spirit of the dish. Crispy fish patties, spiced chutney, and pillowy pav buns come together for a playful twist that still feels true to its street food roots.

Ingredients

1 pound rockfish fillets, minced
1 medium carrot, finely grated
1 small red onion, finely chopped
1 jalapeño, finely chopped
1/4 cup fresh cilantro, chopped
1 teaspoon garam masala
Salt and pepper, to taste
1/2 cup aloo bhujiya (crushed, for texture)
Oil, for frying
6 pav buns (or soft dinner rolls)

 Maggi chutney (or green chutney)
1 tomato, sliced
1 small red onion, thinly sliced
1/2 cup cooked Magginoodles (optional, for garnish)

Preparation

In a large bowl, combine the rockfish, carrot, onion, jalapeño, cilantro, garam masala, salt, and pepper. Mix well, then fold in the aloo bhujiya to bind and add crunch. Form the mixture into small patties, pressing firmly so they hold their shape.



Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the patties until golden brown and cooked through, 3–4 minutes per side. .

Lightly toast the pav buns. Spread each with spicy Maggi chutney, then place a hot fish patty . Top with sliced onion, tomato, and, for a playful street-style flourish, a few cooked Maggi noodles.erve immediately.

title: Indian-Spiced Yellowtail Ceviche
text:
# Indian-Spiced Yellowtail Ceviche

## Description
Ceviche is a dish built on brightness and simplicity, and this version adds an Indian twist with garam masala. Fresh yellowtail is cured in lime juice, then tossed with crisp vegetables, green mango, and herbs for layers of texture and flavor. The spices bring warmth to the sharp acidity, making this fusion ceviche perfect for scooping up with your favorite chips or crackers.

Ingredients

2 shallots
2 green onions
2  chiles

1/4 cup fresh cilantro
Juice of 4 limes

Chips or crackers, for serving

Preparation
In a large mixing bowl, combine the diced yellowtail, shallots, green onions, chilies, cucumber, and cilantro. Pour the lime juice and stir well to coat. Add the garam masala and salt, until evenly seasoned. Cover and refrigerate for  to allow the fish to cure in the lime juice and the flavors to meld.
Serve chilled with chips or crackers for scooping.

title: Keema (Ground Meat)
text:
# Keema (Ground Meat)

## Description
Keema — meaning “minced meat” — is a dish with deep roots across the Indian subcontinent. Introduced during the Mughal era, keema became a staple of royal kitchens, where it was often prepared with lamb, rich spices, and dried fruits. Over time, it made its way into everyday homes, becoming something far more humble and versatile — a spiced ground meat dish cooked with aromatics and often paired with peas to make the popular keema mattar.

Every food culture has its own version of ground meat comfort: burgers, meatballs, kebabs, areyes. For us, it’s keema — deeply spiced, endlessly adaptable, and perfect for whatever game you’ve got on hand. As hunters and anglers, we’re always working with ground venison, wild boar, elk, or bear. This is one of the best ways to turn those packs in the freezer into something bold, filling, and delicious.

This version gives you a base marinade for keema that keeps the meat juicy, tender, and full of flavor. Use it as a jumping-off point — adjust the spice, add onions, garlic, tomatoes, or throw in peas or potatoes depending on the dish you’re aiming for. 

Ingredients: 

1 lb ground game meat 
½ cup yogurt 
2 tablespoons garam masala 
1 tablespoon salt 

In a bowl, combine all the ingredients and mix well until the yogurt and spices are fully worked into the meat. Let it marinate for at least 1 hour — but if you can, give it 24. The yogurt helps tenderize the meat and locks in moisture.

title: Keema Kachori
text:
# Keema Kachori

## Description
If you’ve made the keema base from earlier, here’s one of the best ways to use it — stuffed into dough and deep-fried until golden. Kachori is one of my all-time favorite snacks. It’s simple but perfect: crispy dough on the outside, spicy, juicy filling on the inside.
There are a lot of variations — the most famous being pyaaz (onion) kachori I went with a keema version, using ground deer. You can swap in any ground meat you have on hand. The key is keeping the filling juicy enough to steam inside the dough while it fries.
Paired with a punchy curry leaf chutney, this version takes all the comfort of keema and wraps it into something you can eat with your hands — hot, crispy, and impossible to stop at just one.

Ingredients
For the Keema Filling:
1  ground game meat (deer, boar, venison, or beef)
½ cup yogurt

1 tablespoon ginger garlic paste

1 tablespoon salt
1 tablespoon deggi mirch (or other chili powder)
red onion, finely chopped
cup peas
cup diced eggplant
Oil for cooking

For the Curry Leaf Chutney:
1 cups fresh curry leaves
1 bunch cilantro
1 jalapeño (or more if you want it spicy)
cup shredded coconut
 cup water
Juice of 1 lime
1 teaspoon cumin seeds
1 teaspoon mustard seeds
Oil for tempering

For the Dough:
2 cups all-purpose flour
1 teaspoon salt
 cup oil
 cup water (plus more if needed)

For Frying:
Neutral oil (vocado oil works best)
Preparation
Prepare the Keema Filling:
In a bowl, mix the ground meat with yogurt, ginger garlic paste, salt, and deggi mirch. Let it marinate for at least hour.

Heat oil in a over medium-high. dd the onion and cook until translucent. Add the marinated and cook, stirring occasionally. dd peas and diced eggplant. Cook until the meat is just done but still juicy — don’t let it dry out. Add extra oil if needed, especially if using lean game meat. Let the filling cool completely before using.

Make the Curry Leaf Chutney:
In a blender, combine curry leaves, cilantro, jalapeño, coconut, water, and lime juice. Blend to your preferred consistency.

In a small pan, heat a little oil and toast cumin and mustard seeds until they pop. Stir the tempered seeds into the chutney. Set aside.

Prepare the Dough:
In a mixing bowl, combine the flour and salt. Add oil and water, until you form a soft but slightly firm dough. Add more water if needed. Cover and let it rest for about 1 hour.

Assemble and Fry:
inch off enough dough to form a golf-ball-sized piece. Flatten it out, keeping the center slightly thicker than the edges. Add a spoonful of cooled keema filling. Carefully bring the edges together to enclose the filling, then gently flatten into a 3– round .

Heat oil to 285–315°F. Fry the kachoris slowly0–15 minutes  every 2–3 minutes once they start to floatboth sides are golden and crisp.

Drain on a rack or paper towels. Serve hot with curry leaf chutney.

title: Nandu Rasam with Crab Pakoras
text:
# Nandu Rasam with Crab Pakoras

## Description
This dish is a marriage of two coastal traditions—South Indian nandu rasam (crab rasam) and b bisque. The rasam brings spice, tang, and heat, while the bisque technique lends depth and silkiness. To complete the experience, crispy crab pakoras float on top, adding both crunch and indulgence. It’s comfort food with elegance, a dish that nods to heritage while embracing innovation.

This dish marries South Indian nandu rasam (crab rasam) with French-inspired crab bisque. The rasam brings spice, tang, and heat, while the bisque technique—slowly reducing crab shells and aromatics—adds depth and silkiness. Crispy crab pakoras float on top for crunch and indulgence.

Pakoras are Indian spiced fritters made by coating ingredients in seasoned chickpea flour batter and deep-frying until golden. Traditionally a street food or appetizer featuring vegetables, here we use crab meat for an indulgent twist. The challenge? Keeping them crispy in soup. The carbonated batter creates an extra-light, airy texture that helps these morsels maintain their crunch even as they soak up the spiced broth. It's comfort food with elegance, bridging continents and techniques.

Ingredients
Crab & Pakoras:
1 large Dungeness crab (about 23 pounds)
1 cup chickpea flour (for batter), plus 
2 tablespoons (for binding the meat)
2 green onions, finely sliced
 teaspoon garam masala, divided
Salt, to taste

½ cup lub soda (or carbonated beverage of choice)
Oil, for frying
Rasam:
2 tablespoons Avocado oil
1 red onion, finely chopped
4 garlic cloves, minced
1-inch piece ginger, peeled and minced
1/2 cup tomato puree
2 teaspoons garam masala
1 cinnamon stick
3 whole star anise
810 curry leaves, plus more for garnish
Salt, to taste
1/4 cup heavy cream
To serve: 
Cilantro, optional

Preparation

Start by boiling the crab in a large pot of salted water until fully cooked, about 10–12 minutes. Reserve the cooking liquid. Once cool enough to handle, pick out all the crab meat and set it aside. Do not discard the shells. 

To make the pakoras, combine the crab meat with 2 tablespoons of the chickpea flour, green onions, 1 teaspoon of the garam masala, and the salt. Use your hands to orm small bite-sized balls. In another bowl, whisk together the remaining 1 cup of chickpea flour, garam masala, and just enough club soda to create a thick batter. of oil in a large skillet over medium-high until 350°F (175°C)Dip the crab balls into the batter and fry until golden and crisp. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate and set aside. 

For the rasam, heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic, and ginger, and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in tomato puree, garam masala, cinnamon, star anise, curry leaves, and salt. Cook for 5 minutes dd the reserved crab cooking liquid and immer for 20 minutes.

Add 2 cups of the tomato mixture to a blender along with the reserved crab shells. Blend on medium until smooth Line a fine mesh sieve with cheesecloth and place over the pot with the tomato mixture. Strain the crab shell mixture back into the pot. Discard any solids. Stir in the heavy cream and adjust to taste. The broth should now have the body of a bisque with the spice and aromatics of a rasam.

To serve, place a few hot crab pakoras into each bowl. Ladle the steaming rasam over the top and garnish with fresh curry leaves or cilantro. The pakoras soak up the spiced broth while keeping their crispy edges, making each spoonful both crunchy and soothing.

title: Ponzu Ginger Goose
text:
# Ponzu Ginger Goose

## Description
This goose recipe is inspired by one of my favorite Chinese takeout dishes, Mongolian Beef. 
The goose breasts are first salted and rested, then sliced and seasoned before being briefly fried to achieve a crispy exterior while remaining tender inside. The accompanying sauce, a harmonious blend of caramelized onion, aromatic ginger and garlic, and a balance of Worcestershire and Ponzu, is enhanced with a touch of brown sugar for depth and richness. Finished with a brief simmer, this dish is perfect served over rice, with a sprinkle of furikake and a kick of pickled chilies. 





Ingredients
2 goose breast 
Salt, to taste
1 tablespoon pepper 
1/2 cup cornstarch 
1/2 cup all-purpose flour 
1 large egg
Avocado oil 
1 onion 
1/2-inch piece fresh ginger 
4 garlic cloves
1/2 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce
2 tablespoons Ponzu Sauce 
1/2 tablespoon brown sugar
Furikake, for serving
Pickled chilies, for serving
Preparation
Start by salting the goose breasts and allowing them to rest in the refrigerator for 3-5 hours. Rinse off the salt and slice the breasts into thin strips, about 1/8-inch. Toss the strips with a tablespoon of freshly cracked pepper.

In a shallow bowl, thoroughly combine the cornstarch and flour. In another shallow bowl, beat the egg, add the goose strips, and toss to coat evenly. Dredge the coated strips in the cornstarch-flour mixture, shaking off any excess flour.  

Heat the avocado oil in a pan and fry the goose strips for one minute on each side, aiming for a crispy exterior while leaving the inside slightly undercooked; the goose will finish cooking in the sauce.

For the sauce, heat 1 tablespoon of avocado oil in a pan and sauté the onion until it begins to caramelize. Add the ginger and garlic, cooking them down until fragrant, about 1 minute. Then, incorporate the Worcestershire sauce and Ponzu sauce and cook, stirring often, until reduced by half, about 10 minutes. Stir in the brown sugar and let it dissolve completely.

To assemble, add the goose strips to the sauce, ensuring each piece is well coated. Simmer over low heat for 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. Serve over rice, garnished with furikake and pickled chilies.

title: Stuffed Crab (Caranguejos Recheados)
text:
# Stuffed Crab (Caranguejos Recheados)

## Description
Caranguejos Recheados is a dish that beautifully encapsulates the rich culinary heritage of Goa, blending local flavors with Portuguese influences. This spicy, stuffed crab is a true testament to the vibrant culture of the coastal region. 
The filling, a flavorful blend of aromatic spices like garam masala, turmeric, and amchoor, paired with onions, tomatoes, garlic, and ginger, creates a symphony of tastes that are both comforting and exotic. 
Caranguejos Recheados is more than just a dish—it’s a culinary experience that transports you straight to the heart of Goa.




Ingredients
1 medium Dungeness crab (about 2 to 3 pounds)
2 tablespoons oil (such as vegetable oil or coconut oil)
2 tablespoons mustard seeds
1 red onion, finely chopped
8 garlic cloves, minced
1/2-inch piece fresh ginger, minced
3 small tomatoes, finely chopped
2 tablespoons garam masala
2 teaspoons amchoor 
1 teaspoon turmeric powder
Salt, to taste
1 pinch black pepper
Breadcrumbs, for topping
Preparation
Start by boiling the Dungeness crab in a large pot of salted water. Boil until the crab is fully cooked, 10-15. Allow the crab to cool slightly before carefully extracting the meat from the shell. Be sure to keep the shell intact, as you’ll be using it later for stuffing. Set the crab meat aside while you prepare the masala.

In a large pan, heat about 2 tablespoons of oil over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and cook undisturbed until they splutter and release their aromatic oils, about X minutes. 

Next, add the finely chopped onions and sauté them until they turn golden brown. Stir in the minced garlic and ginger, and cook until the fragrance fills your kitchen, 1-2 minutes. Now, add the chopped tomatoes, allowing them to soften and meld into the mixture stirring frequently for 5-7 minutes. At this point, sprinkle in the garam masala, amchoor, turmeric, salt, and a pinch of black pepper. Stir the spices into the mixture and cook until the masala thickens into a rich paste, about 10 minutes. Gently fold the crab meat into the masala, ensuring that each piece is thoroughly coated with the spiced mixture. Cook for another 5 minutes (this gives the flavors time to meld). Taste the mixture and adjust the seasoning if needed.

Preheat your oven to 350°F. Spoon the prepared crab masala mixture back into the empty crab shell, packing it tightly. Finish by sprinkling a generous layer of bread crumbs on top for a crispy texture. Place the stuffed crab on a baking tray and bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the breadcrumbs turn a golden brown.

Once baked to perfection, remove the crab from the oven and let it cool slightly before serving. Enjoy this rich, spicy dish with buttered toast or your favorite sides to soak up every bit of the flavorful sauce.

title: Venison Curry
text:
# Venison Curry

## Description
This recipe uses sous vide as a technique to foolproof your lean wild game, ensuring it’s perfectly tender and evenly cooked every time. The flavors of yogurt, garlic, and a blend of aromatic spices like garam masala and turmeric infuse the meat while it marinates, creating a complex flavor profile that is then enhanced by a sear for a beautifully caramelized crust. 

The curry base, a harmonious mix of cumin, mustard seeds, and fresh ginger, provides an aromatic and vibrant complement to the venison. Serve this exquisite dish with your favorite bread, roti, or rice.








Ingredients
1 Venison Tenderloin 
Marinade:
1 cup plain yogurt
1 tablespoon garam masala
1 teaspoon turmeric
4 cloves garlic, minced
Salt, to taste
Pepper, to taste
Curry:
2 tablespoons oil
1 teaspoon mustard seeds
1 teaspoon cumin seeds
1 red onion, minced
2 tomatoes, finely chopped
1 bunch cilantro 
1-inch piece fresh ginger, minced
4 cloves garlic, minced
1 lime

Preparation
To begin, prepare your deer tenderloin by trimming off any silver skin. In a large bowl, combine the plain yogurt, garam masala, turmeric, garlic, salt, and pepper. Coat the tenderloin with the yogurt mixture, ensuring it's thoroughly covered. Place the tenderloin in a Ziploc bag, ensuring all air is removed, and let it marinate in the refrigerator for 6 to 24 hours.

When you would like to cook the venison, preheat a water bath to 120°F (49°C) using your sous vide. Submerge the bag with the marinated venison in the water bath, and let it cook for 4 hours. With 30 minutes left on the meat, prepare the curry base. Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Once shimmering, add the mustard seeds and cumin seeds, and cook until golden brown and sizzling, about 3 minutes. Add the onion, tomatoes, cilantro stems, and ginger to the pan, and sauté until the mixture becomes soft and fragrant, about 5 to 7 minutes. Then, add minced garlic and cook for another minute.

Remove the venison from the water bath (at this point it should have cooked for 4 hours total and should read 120°F (49°C) at its thickest point). Discard the plastic bag and pat the meat dry with paper towels. Cut the tenderloin into bite-sized pieces. In a separate pan, heat oil over high heat and sear the venison pieces on all sides until a brown crust forms, about 2 to 3 minutes per side. Add the venison to the pan with the curry mixture and stir well to combine. Turn the heat to medium and simmer for about 10 minutes, giving the flavors time to meld together. Remove from the heat and ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh cilantro and lime wedges. Serve with your choice of bread, roti, or rice.

title: Wild Boar Breakfast Pizza
text:
# Wild Boar Breakfast Pizza

## Description
When the craving for pizza meets the call for breakfast, this dish brings the best of both worlds together. A base of sharp cheddar-topped dough bakes until crisp, then gets layered with creamy country-style gravy made from wild boar breakfast sausage. Cracked eggs finish cooking right on top, their yolks still runny for richness. A final hit of lemon zest cuts through the indulgence, creating a pizza that’s hearty, playful, and perfect for any time of day.

Ingredients
1 ball pizza dough
2 cups sharp cheddar cheese 
1 pound wild boar breakfast sausage (or deer country sausage)
2 tablespoons flour
2 cups whole milk
Salt and pepper, to taste
1 teaspoon Aleppo pepper (optional)
4 eggs
Zest of 1 lemon
Preparation
Preheat oven to 500–550°F. Roll out the pizza dough and place it on a baking stone or sheet. Top with shredded cheddar and bake until nearly, but not fully, cooked through.
Meanwhile, prepare the gravy. Heat avocado oil in a skillet over medium heat. dd the sausage and cook until about 90% done. Stir in the flour and cook for 1–2 minutes to form a roux, then gradually whisk in the milk. Simmer, stirring often, until thick and creamy. Season with salt, pepper, and Aleppo pepper if using.
Remove the pizza from the oven and spoon the sausage gravy evenly over the top. Crack the eggs directly onto the pizza, spacing them out so each slice will hold some yolk. Return the pizza to the oven and bake until the whites are set but the yolks remain runny, about 4–6 minutes.
 with fresh lemon zest. Slice and serve immediately, enjoying the blend of molten cheese, savory gravy, and rich egg yolk on crisp crust.

title: Wild Boar Mirchi Bajji
text:
# Wild Boar Mirchi Bajji

## Description
This recipe is a flavorful twist on Mirchi Baji, a popular Indian street food made with green chilies dipped in a spiced chickpea flour batter and fried until crispy. Traditionally, Mirchi Bajji uses long green peppers like banana or bhavnagri chilies, but here, we’re elevating the dish by using Anaheim peppers and stuffing them with a savory boar sausage mixture. The result is a heartier and less spicy version of the classic snack, perfect as an appetizer or a fun side dish.








Ingredients
NAME:
Oil, for frying
1 teaspoon mustard seeds
8-10 curry leaves
1 pound ground boar (or boar sausage, seasoned with garam masala)
1 medium onion, finely chopped
2 tablespoons garam masala (if using plain ground boar)
Salt, to taste
6-8 large Anaheim chiles
Batter:
1 cup chickpea flour 
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/4 teaspoon black pepper
Tamarind Yogurt Dipping Sauce:
1/2 cup plain yogurt
1 tablespoon tamarind paste
1 teaspoon sugar
Salt, to taste
Fresh cilantro, for garnish
Preparation
Start by heating oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Once the oil is hot, add the mustard seeds and curry leaves, allowing them to crackle. Add finely chopped onion and sauté until it turns golden and caramelized. Stir in the ground boar and cook, stirring often, until the meat is fully cooked, about 10-15 minutes. Set the boar mixture aside to cool.

Next, prepare the Anaheim chiles by making a lengthwise slit in each starting just below the top and stopping just before the tip. Gently open the peppers and carefully stuff them with the cooled boar mixture.

To make the batter, combine the chickpea flour, salt, and pepper in a shallow bowl. Gradually whisk in water until you form a thick, smooth batter that clings to the peppers without dripping (about 2 cups). Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pan. Dip each stuffed pepper into the batter, ensuring they’re fully coated, and fry until crispy and golden brown. Remove and drain on paper towels.

For the tamarind yogurt dipping sauce, mix the yogurt, tamarind paste, sugar, and salt until smooth. Adjust seasoning if necessary. Serve the fried stuffed peppers hot with the dipping sauce and garnish with fresh cilantro.
